+# Acceptance Criteria
+
+Rules:
+
+- Criteria lines use the exact format `- ACn: <criterion>`.
+- Every criterion ends with [verify: exec `<command>`],
+  [verify: invariant `<command>`], [verify: judged] or
+  [verify: none — <reason>].
+- After `flow freeze` this file is checksum-protected: any edit outside
+  `keryx flow ac update` fails every gate and status transition.
+- Completion requires every ACn to be confirmed via
+  `keryx flow ac confirm <id> <ACn>`.
+
+## Criteria
+
+- AC1: When the pull request is open with the reviewed base and a different head, the `desk-publish` preview returns `headMoved` with both commits, verdict `comment`, inline off, and a body whose first line names the reviewed commit and says the pull request moved on; submit posts a `COMMENT` review with `commit_id` equal to the reviewed head. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/desk-publication.test.ts`]
+- AC2: With a moved head, a submit whose settings ask for another verdict or inline comments still posts a `COMMENT` with no inline comments; a head that moved again after the preview fails with `stale:` and posts nothing; automatic publication with a moved head posts nothing; a changed base or a closed pull request keeps today's refusal. · sensitive: failure-scenario [verify: exec `bun test src/review/desk-publication.test.ts`]
+- AC3: The publish dialog with a moved head shows both commits, disables the verdict choice and inline comments, and labels the as-is action "Publish as is for" the short reviewed commit; with the current head the dialog is unchanged. [verify: exec `sh -c 'cd apps/desktop && bun test src/reviews/ReviewPanel.dom.test.tsx'`]
+- AC4: `on_head_move` has the values `ask`, `follow`, `ignore`; a manual review defaults to `ask` and a rule-triggered review to `follow`; a missing or unknown stored value reads as the default. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/head-move.test.ts`]
+- AC5: The previous-attempt selection accepts the newest partial attempt with accepted findings and an attempt run with different settings, and rejects imported, failed, cancelled and unreviewed attempts. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/update-round.test.ts`]
+- AC6: `findPreviousRound` still chooses a previous round recorded under different review settings. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/prior-round.test.ts`]
+- AC7: A new attempt on a newer head of the same Review (stage 2 round N+1, started by "Review again" / "New review round" or "Update review") builds on the previous round: after a partial previous round with accepted findings it runs in mode delta with a non-empty prior-findings list and the area the partial round did not cover planned as unreviewed; after a previous round run with different settings it still gets the previous findings; the previous-attempt rule exists once (selectPriorAttempt), the old options-key rule is gone. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/prior-round.test.ts src/review/update-round.test.ts src/review/desk-run-service.test.ts src/review/desk-run-executor.test.ts`]
+- AC8: Backend review tests, the Desktop review suites, typecheck and lint pass on the branch; this flow leaves the attention-set code, attachBadges/localBadge and the toolbar container queries as stage 2 left them. [verify: invariant `sh -c 'bun test src/review && cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review src/reviews && cd ../.. && bun run typecheck && bunx eslint src/review apps/desktop/src/review && git diff --quiet 98bec59046d0ce30500b341e8c18ba5b767069bb -- apps/desktop/src/review/ReviewBoard.tsx src/review/board-badges.ts src/review/desk-run-store.ts apps/desktop/src/styles/review.css'`]
+- AC9: The scenario on a real pull request with a commit pushed during a round, then published as is from Desktop. [verify: judged]
+- AC10: In the publish dialog with a moved head, "Update review to <sha>" starts a new round of the same Review on the current head; the keep/dismiss answers given in the previous round's draft are pre-selected in the new round's publication draft for findings with the same finding id. [verify: exec `sh -c 'bun test src/review/desk-publication.test.ts && cd apps/desktop && bun test src/reviews src/review'`]

+# Desktop Review v2 stage 3: head move
+
+## Problem
+
+When the head of a pull request moves after a Desktop review finished, the review can no longer be published at all: `desk-publish` reports "The pull request is closed or its revision moved" and only a local save remains (spec O8). There is no `on_head_move` setting, and "Review again" starts an unrelated run instead of an update round of the same review. The previous-round rules reject a partial round and a round run with different settings (spec O10).
+
+Source: `docs/requirements/keryx-desktop-review-v2/` (PRD R9, R10; specification "Поведение при смене head"; implementation plan v0.1.3, stage 3, owner decisions D1 and D2).
+
+## Expected outcome
+
+1. The publish dialog offers the D1 variants when the head moved after the reviewed commit: "Publish as is for `<sha>`" is allowed only with the verdict Comment and a first body line that names the reviewed commit and says the pull request moved on. Save locally and Skip stay as they are. Automatic publication still refuses a moved head.
+2. `on_head_move` exists as a typed setting with the values `ask`, `follow`, `ignore`; a manual review defaults to `ask` (D2), a rule-triggered review to `follow`.
+3. "Review again" becomes an update round of the same Review (blocked on stage 2, see below).
+4. The previous-round choice accepts a partially completed round and a round run with other settings, with tests.
+
+## Dependency on stage 2
+
+Stage 3 requires stage 2 (flow 519, branch `feat/desktop-review-v2-stage2`): the update round belongs to the Review entity and its rounds, which stage 2 introduces. The operator chose to start stage 3 before stage 2 lands. Items 1, 2 and the round-independent part of 4 are built first, shaped so they attach to rounds without a rewrite. Item 3 and the parts of item 4 that need rounds (wiring the selection into the run start, the package trust rule) wait for stage 2's rounds migration; this flow records them as blocked until then. No rounds schema is invented here.
+
+## Out of scope
+
+- The Reviews tab, the `reviews` table and the migration (stage 2).
+- Wave-boundary head checks in the executor and the `review-orchestrator` "Head moved" procedure (stage 4 for the skill; executor checks go with item 3).
+- Carrying finding answers across the update round (goes with item 3).

 Enable **Publish to GitHub automatically** in **Run review** to post one

 ### Watch PRs while Desktop is closed
 
 From **Review**, open **PR watcher**, choose a polling interval and select **Enable watcher**. The default is five minutes. The first successful poll records which PRs are open, their revisions, requested reviewers and CI. The history shows the 50 latest changes with the time Keryx observed them.
 
 Connect your account in **Settings → Integrations** so the background process can read the repository after your shell exits. macOS runs the schedule while you are logged in and the Mac is awake. You can quit Keryx Desktop. If the timer needs repair after an upgrade or a local tool moves, open **PR watcher** and select **Restore timer**. After sleep or a failed poll, the watcher compares the next complete result with the last successful one. Open **PR watcher** to check the timer, last attempt and last success, or select **Pause watcher**. **Resume watcher** starts with a fresh baseline so changes that occurred during an explicit pause do not appear as new events.
 
 Keeping the same GitHub account preserves an existing schedule. Changing
 accounts or disconnecting pauses the previous watcher and clears its pending
 automatic reviews. Enable the watcher under the new account when ready.
 
 ### Set up automatic PR reviews
 
 Open **Review → Review rules → New rule** and choose **Review requested or re-requested** or **New head commit**. You can restrict a rule to a PR author, assignee or requested reviewer. For a team, enter its GitHub slug, such as `my-org/frontend`. **Wait for passing CI** holds the request until checks pass on the current revision. Read the preview and set a time limit. Leave **Token limit (optional)** blank for unlimited tokens, or enter a positive whole number to cap each review. Save the rule.
 
 Enable **PR watcher** to run the rules on its local schedule. Use a Keryx model provider signed in for noninteractive use by the local CLI. The timer can use stored credentials after Desktop exits. Credentials available only in an interactive terminal are outside its environment. The next complete poll establishes a baseline when you enable or edit a rule. Changes already present at that poll are skipped. A temporary connection error leaves pending work in place until the watcher can verify the repository again.
